clinician.trajectory_summary: A 76-year-old man presented with a 5-year history of an intermittent erythematous, granulomatous, discoid plaques rash, accompanied by normocytic anaemia, thrombocytopenia, and elevated inflammatory markers. Initial skin biopsy showed a superficial dermal inflammatory infiltrate, with differential diagnoses including Sweet’s syndrome. The condition progressed with the reappearance of the rash and new-onset inflammatory arthritis, fatigue, and joint pain, which had temporary relief with I.M. Depomedrone. A second skin biopsy confirmed histiocytoid Sweet’s syndrome. The patient was then placed on long-term Prednisolone, to which he responded very well, with complete clearing of the rash and resolution of shoulder pain. Despite this initial response, subsequent genetic testing identified a pathogenic variant in the UBA1 gene, confirming the diagnosis of VEXAS.
